issues.problem: The selected trade and the offer list reach the client through `ContainerData`, which vanilla sends as 16-bit shorts (`ClientboundContainerSetDataPacket`). Index 16 holds `ENERGY_PER_TRADE` = 1,000,000 internal units, which gets truncated, so the GUI shows the wrong trade CE. Items are sent as raw registry int IDs plus a count, so data components are lost. For example, a librarian's enchanted book or an armorer's enchanted armour shows as a plain item, and costs with components are shown wrongly. Also, every `get(index)` call runs `offer()`/`offerCount()`, each doing a new entity AABB search, so each open menu does about 37 entity searches every tick. The menu GameTest reads the server-side ContainerData directly, so none of this is caught.
issues.reason: AC-F026-002 requires the GUI to show the selected trade and its required materials correctly. ContainerData is meant only for small int values; full ItemStacks and long values need proper stream codecs.
issues.fix: Send the merchant's offers (e.g. `MerchantOffers.STREAM_CODEC` or ItemStack/ItemCost stream codecs for the visible offers) plus the selected index, state and long CE values with a clientbound payload or the menu's extra data when they change. Keep ContainerData only for values that fit in 16 bits. Look up the merchant once per server tick instead of once per data index. Make the GameTest check the values the client screen actually receives.

history.note: fixed: Replaced offer data encoded as short values and item IDs with a MerchantOffers client payload carrying full stacks and long CE values. The GameTest checks a codec round trip.

ContainerData is replaced by a TradeSnapshotPayload using MerchantOffers.STREAM_CODEC and VAR_LONG values, sent when the content hash changes. The merchant is cached once per tick. The GameTest round-trips the codec and checks components, discounted costs and the long CE value.

issues.problem: `/item replace block 0 100 0 container.N` needs the block entity to be a vanilla `Container`. `AutoTraderBlockEntity` only has an `ItemStackHandler`, so these commands fail and the materials and fuel are never placed. If they did work, the device ticks `tryTrade` every tick, so during the 10-tick wait it would complete the trade (the compressed energetic clay gives exactly 1,000,000 internal CE) and use up the inputs before the screenshot. Either way, the screenshot does not show the intended selected trade with its required materials. It also shows no stop condition, and with only one offer it does not show a trade list or a selection.
issues.reason: The E2E is the only evidence for the screen part of AC-F026-002, which asks for a capture of the trade list with the selected trade and its required materials shown correctly.
issues.fix: Fill the device in a way that works for an ItemHandler-only block entity, for example from a vanilla chest or hopper next to it, or through player inventory clicks in the GUI. Give the villager several offers, select a non-first offer through the GUI, and set up a stop condition (e.g. missing material or no CE) so the screenshot shows the list, the highlighted selection, the current discounted required materials and the stop state without the trade consuming them.

history.note: fixed: The E2E now fills the block entity through NBT, presents two offers, selects the discounted second offer and leaves trading stopped for the screenshot.

The E2E fills the block entity via NBT merge, spawns two offers, and clicks the second one in the GUI. With no fuel the device stops for lack of CE, so nothing is consumed. The click at (700,291) lands on the second offer button at GUI scale 1, assuming MC Pilot runs at that scale; I did not confirm the scale.

issues.problem: `level.sendBlockUpdated(...)` is called on every state change, but the block entity does not override `getUpdatePacket`/`getUpdateTag`, so nothing is synced. The call only forces useless block updates and re-renders, up to once per tick while the state changes.
issues.reason: The code style says to remove code the current behaviour does not use. The client gets its data only through the menu.
issues.fix: Replace `setChangedAndSync()` with a plain `setChanged()` (or sync through the menu as described above) and remove the `sendBlockUpdated` call.

history.note: fixed: Removed the block update call; state changes use setChanged(), and the open menu supplies client updates.
setChangedAndSync and sendBlockUpdated are gone from the trade package; state changes call setChanged().
